title: Supported signed-twist Hom groups and their canonical operations
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $P$ and $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], with the signed finite Tate sheaves $A_X(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Select either the small etale site ($\mathrm{pro}=\mathrm{false}$) or the small pro-etale site ($\mathrm{pro}=\mathrm{true}$). Use the corresponding category of $A$-module sheaves, its derived category and its degree-zero embedding. The pro-etale constant and twist sheaves are the exact comparison inverse images of the etale ones; use that same exact comparison functor.

For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] and integers $a,r$, define the supported signed-twist Hom group
$$H_i^a(X,A(r)):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(i_*A_Z[0],A_X(r)[a]),$$
and define the ordinary Hom group by replacing $i_*A_Z$ with $A_X$. Here $i_*$ is the underived direct image. Forget support by precomposition with the degree-zero image of the restriction $A_X\to i_*A_Z$.

Use the normalized signed-twist tensor multiplication $A_X(r)\otimes_A A_X(s)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(r+s)$: on positive powers it is the ordered tensor-power identification, at weight zero it is the unitor, and on opposite powers it is evaluation against the dual. Also retain this same multiplication for a commutative coefficient ring $A$ annihilated by any positive integer $m$ invertible on $X$, using the finite root sheaf $\mu_m\otimes_{\mathbb Z/m}A$. On the pro-etale site transport the etale multiplication through the strong monoidal comparison.

For $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, closed $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, define the internal product by the tensor-morphism construction of [def-pur-supported-cup], followed by the shifted normalized twist multiplication. Its output has support $Z\times_X W$, degree $a+b$ and twist $r+s$. On the etale site use the identical degree-zero coefficient multiplication and right-shift-first tensor comparison.

For a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with closed $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:Z'\hookrightarrow Y$, $v:Y\to X$ and $g:Z'\to Z$, define supported pullback by exact derived inverse image, precomposed with the inverse of the closed-constant exchange $v^*i_*A_Z\cong j_*A_{Z'}$ normalized by restriction of the coefficient unit, and followed by the degree-zero, shift and canonical twist-pullback comparisons. For two closed immersions $i:C\hookrightarrow X$, $j:D\hookrightarrow X$ and $g:D\to C$ with $g i=j$, define change of support $H_j^a(X,A(r))\to H_i^a(X,A(r))$ by precomposition with the degree-zero image of the unique restriction $i_*A_C\to j_*A_D$ commuting with the coefficient-unit restrictions. These are the already constructed canonical maps, with no functoriality or product laws asserted as part of this definition.
